sentence: This project builds question answering data and methods that make electronic health record systems easier to use, balancing trust with performance.
This project builds detailed maps of the pathways inside and outside the cerebellar connectome, checked by experts, to help study health and disease.
This project builds genetic tools to study a major group of neurons in the outermost layer of the cortex, which receives top-down information.
This project tries to revive old antimicrobial agents by combining two materials at the nanometer scale to fight open fracture infections.
This project studies how intestinal stem cells keep a memory of past inflammation that changes their ability to regenerate the intestinal lining.
This project tests small molecules that act against melanoma in mice to find out how they work in additional models.
This project studies how the estrogen receptor gene and the Hippo pathway work together.
This project tries to improve treatment of glioblastoma by combining Chimeric Antigen Receptor T cell therapy with biomaterials.
This project studies the pathways that control whole body regeneration in the planarian flatworm and the acoel.
This project builds sensitive methods to measure metals in environmental and biological samples and to study harmful health effects using microbiome approaches.
This project tries to change how sensitive prostate cancer is to androgen receptor inhibition by changing chemical signaling in the microenvironment.
This project studies how an HIV protein called integrase interacts with the RNA of the virus.
This project studies how the loss of myelin changes motor coding and movement in behavior, using imaging and electrical recording.
This project uses computer simulations and bioinformatics to study the structures of complex glycans and how proteins recognize them.
This project studies how neuroimmune signaling and norepinephrine release relate to stress and opioid misuse.
This project tries to find the unknown receptors on phagocytic cells that respond to a don't-eat-me signal that helps leukemia cells escape the immune system.
This project develops imaging and analysis methods to measure indicators of intestinal health and disease in premature infants with necrotizing enterocolitis.
This project uses imaging mass cytometry to study immune cells in gut mucosa samples to understand immune responses to Shigella.
